Hi Liam —

Great to hear about the uptake. Quick summary and three options attached below (SOW + order form attached):

1) Committed increase to 6M tokens / month — 12-month term discount applied (effective on next billing cycle). Includes 10% burst pocket (600k tokens) billed at discounted overage rate and automatic soft-throttle that gracefully reduces concurrency by route when sustained overage is detected.

2) Short-term top-up (3-month) — commit to 4M tokens for three months with a larger burst pocket (20%) and no long-term discount. Useful if you want to bridge to a larger annual commit.

3) Conservative approach — keep 2M commit, add paid burst-only buffer (pre-purchased credits) and enable prefix caching + KV suggestions to reduce unit spend.

Lead time: changes typically take 48–72 hours to reflect in provisioning for hosted accounts. For contract updates we can do an addendum signed via DocuSign — I attached a draft order form.

Procurement note (you can copy this): "When a customer exceeds their committed token allowance, Redwood applies the configured burst pocket first. If burst credits are exhausted, soft-throttle policies reduce per-route concurrency and apply a graceful rate limit; requests receive 429s only after the soft-throttle thresholds are exceeded or a hard overage policy is in effect. Customers can elect automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant to avoid 429s while preserving throughput. All events are logged in the Console audit trail for billing and compliance review."

Next step: if option 1 looks good I'll loop in Legal/Finance for an addendum and draft the order form for signature.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Renewals
Redwood Inference
